A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SIMBENCH and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Sections and Appendices A–N can be matched reliably; v4 adds Appendix O.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 45 LLMs, elicitation and quantization comparisons, demographic analyses, regressions, and a Centaur case study.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results and adds uncertainty reporting and a country-level analysis of benchmark composition.

M1.justification: The simulation and elicitation procedures remain unchanged: demographic conditioning, first-token probabilities for base models, and verbalized distributions for instruction-tuned models. No new simulator, training objective, or algorithmic component is introduced; the scoring revision concerns evaluation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 20 datasets and the same population-level and demographic-conditioned tasks. Appendix O describes existing geographic coverage rather than adding populations or scenarios. Dataset-card corrections do not establish changed evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: The 45-model comparison, uniform baseline, token-probability versus verbalized elicitation comparison, and Llama/Minitaur/Centaur case study retain their comparator membership. Newly cited approaches are not newly evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 3 substantively revises the reported scoring protocol. Whereas v1 gives normalization by each question's human-to-uniform TVD, v4 specifies normalization by the dataset-level mean baseline and averaging the resulting test-case scores. This affects the benchmark's central metric, although unchanged leaderboard values do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix O and Section 2.2 quantify geographic balance through country-level counts and Western sample shares. Existing quantization, elicitation, alternative-metric, entropy, mediation, and Centaur analyses are retained. The expanded mechanism discussion does not add corresponding experimental tests.

E5.justification: v4 adds 95% confidence intervals to demographic contrasts in Table 2 and confidence bands to Figure 2. Existing Appendix H significance analyses remain, while Figure 4's standard-error explanation is removed. No increase in runs or new seed information is reported.

E6.justification: Section 4.2 corrects reported scores, including o4-mini low/high from 28.20/29.54 to 27.77/28.99, matching Table 7 already present in v1. The below-uniform model count changes from nine to ten, and geographic counts are newly reported. The main leaderboard and rankings remain unchanged; these are not demonstrated performance improvements.

T1.justification: New Equation 2 supplies a non-equivalent operational definition of the score using a dataset-level denominator and explains the undefined pointwise case when human responses are uniform. This is a localized mathematical revision; the regression and mediation equations and KL-based reasoning otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The benchmark contribution and headline findings remain: limited simulation fidelity, log-linear scaling, little benefit from inference-time compute, the alignment–plurality tradeoff, demographic difficulties, and capability correlations. Calling the retained 40.80 score 'meaningful but modest' reframes the same result rather than establishing a new core contribution.

C2.justification: v4 substantially expands interpretation: Section 4.3 connects task differences to a value–action gap and restrictions from alignment, whereas v1 mainly reports heterogeneous performance. Section 4.2 replaces optimistic extrapolation from scaling with diminishing returns and qualifications about sparse model families and limited compute comparisons. These revise the implications drawn from largely unchanged evidence.

D1.justification: v4 adds explicit single-token option mapping and score-aggregation details and corrects dataset-card metadata, including WisdomOfCrowds' question count to match the existing sampling table. Conversely, Figure 4 no longer specifies 25 bins. Hardware, quantization, prompts, and the code/data destinations were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: v4 adds literature on first-token mismatch, value–action gaps, counter-normative simulation, and persona control, including Wang et al. (2024), Shen et al. (2025), and Dong et al. (2026). Some citations, including Rescala et al. (2024), are removed. The central positioning as a standardized group-level simulation benchmark is retained.

P1.justification: The main text receives language tightening, localized paragraph rewrites, corrected cross-references, and revised subsection wording. The conclusion gains future work, acknowledgments are added, and Appendix O is introduced. The six-question narrative and most appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds the multipage country table, adds confidence bands to Figure 2, expands Table 2 with interval notation, and revises Figure 4's caption. Conference headers, page numbers, and text reflow alter layout, but the existing visual framework and other plots are retained.

improvement.justification: v4 improves reproducibility through the explicit operational scoring formula, strengthens uncertainty reporting in Figure 2 and Table 2, and reconciles several prose results with existing tables. These are useful, bounded gains. They are partly offset by stronger interpretations of unchanged task comparisons, especially the value–action-gap claim in Section 4.3, which the reported experiments do not directly test.
